cat > .github/workflows/triage.yml <<'EOF'
---
name: triage

# pull_request_target gives a writable token to pull requests from forks.
# It runs with the base repository's privileges, so this workflow must never
# check out, build or run anything from the pull request.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Welcome and label
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
    steps:
      - name: Add the needs-triage label
        run: |
          gh api --silent "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$PR_NUMBER/labels" \
            -f 'labels[]=needs-triage'

      # The title and username are untrusted input. They reach the script only
      # through environment variables, never through ${{ }} inside "run".
      - name: Post the welcome comment
        env:
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          # The title goes in an indented code block so that mentions, links
          # and markup in it stay inert. Line breaks would end the block.
          title=$(printf '%s' "$PR_TITLE" | tr '\r\n' '  ')
          body=$(printf 'Welcome, @%s, and thank you for contributing!\n\n**Summary of this pull request:**\n\n    %s\n' \
            "$PR_AUTHOR" "$title")
          gh api --silent "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments" \
            -f body="$body"
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='README.md'
s=open(p).read()
s+='''
## Pull request triage

The [triage workflow](.github/workflows/triage.yml) runs when a pull request is
opened, including from a fork. It:

- applies the `needs-triage` label
- posts a comment that welcomes the author by username and repeats the pull
  request title as a summary

It does not run again on new commits, title edits or reopening.

### Setup

- Create the `needs-triage` label in the repository before relying on the
  workflow.
- The workflow takes effect once it is on the default branch. The pull request
  that adds it will not be triaged.

### Security notes for maintainers

The workflow uses `pull_request_target`, because the `pull_request` token is
read-only for forks and could not comment or label. This event runs with the
base repository's privileges, even for pull requests from strangers. When
editing the workflow:

- Do not check out, build or run code from the pull request.
- Do not put `${{ }}` expressions containing pull request data in a `run`
  script. Pass them through `env` and quote the variables.
- Keep the title inside the code block, so that it cannot mention people or add
  links and formatting to the bot's comment.
- Keep permissions to the minimum (`pull-requests: write`).
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
actionlint; echo "actionlint=$?"; zizmor --offline .github/workflows/ 2>&1
# dry run of the run scripts with a stub gh and hostile input
d=$(mktemp -d); printf '#!/bin/bash\nprintf "ARG<%%s>\\n" "$@"\n' > $d/gh; chmod +x $d/gh
python3 -I - "$d" <<'EOF'
import yaml,subprocess,sys,os
d=sys.argv[1]
for s in yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/triage.yml'))['jobs']['triage']['steps']:
    r=subprocess.run(['bash','-eo','pipefail','-c',s['run']],env={'PATH':d+':'+os.environ['PATH'],'GITHUB_REPOSITORY':'o/r','PR_NUMBER':'7','PR_AUTHOR':'octocat','PR_TITLE':'"; echo PWNED $(id) `id` @org/team %s\r\n# x'},capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=d)
    print(r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr)
EOF
rm -r "$d"; git status --short

content.text:
I added the triage workflow in `.github/workflows/triage.yml` and documented it in the README. Nothing is committed, and it hasn't run on GitHub.

**What it does:** when a pull request is opened, it applies `needs-triage` and posts a comment that welcomes the author by `@username` and repeats the title as a summary.

**Forks:** it uses `pull_request_target`, because the ordinary `pull_request` trigger only gets a read-only token for fork PRs. The new trigger is risky if misused, so the workflow is limited as follows:
- It never checks out or runs code from the pull request.
- Its only permission is `pull-requests: write`.
- The title and username reach the script as environment variables, so a title can't inject shell commands.
- The title appears in a code block, so it can't `@mention` people or add links to the bot's comment.

**Checks:**
- `actionlint` passed.
- I ran both scripts locally with a stand-in for `gh` and a title full of shell syntax and a line break. Nothing in the title was executed, and it stayed on one line inside the code block.
- `zizmor` reports one high-severity `dangerous-triggers` finding on `pull_request_target`. It flags any use of that trigger, and fork support needs it here. I didn't suppress it, so if your CI runs `zizmor`, you'll need to decide whether to add an ignore comment.

**Before relying on it:**
1. Create the `needs-triage` label in the repository, for example with `gh label create needs-triage`.
2. Merge the workflow into `main`. It only takes effect from the default branch, so the PR that adds it won't be triaged.
3. Open a test PR from a fork and confirm both the label and the comment appear. This is the part I couldn't verify locally.

It runs only when a PR is first opened, not on new commits, title edits or reopening.
